_meta.indication: Treatment of adult patients with metastatic NSCLC whose tumors are ROS1-positive; and treatment of adult and pediatric patients 12 years and older with NTRK gene fusion-positive solid tumors (accelerated approval)

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Pooled ROS1 primary efficacy set from ALKA, STARTRK-1 and STARTRK-2
pivotal_trials.phase: Phase 2 basket study (STARTRK-2) pooled with dose-escalation/activity-estimating trials
pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, single-arm, open-label, dose escalation and/or activity-estimating trials (pooled)
pivotal_trials.population: First 51 consecutively enrolled patients with ROS1 fusion-positive metastatic NSCLC who had not received prior ROS1 TKI, with measurable disease per RECIST v1.1 and ECOG PS ≤ 2
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Confirmed overall response rate (ORR) per blinded independent central review (BICR), with duration of response (DOR) as key secondary
pivotal_trials.result: Confirmed ORR per BICR 78% (95% CI: 65%, 89%); estimated median DOR 15.7 months (95% CI: 11.4, 34.8)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥20%) were fatigue, constipation, dysgeusia, edema, dizziness, diarrhea, nausea, dysesthesia, dyspnea. Grade 3 or 4 adverse reactions occurred in 60% of patients. Serious CNS effects, congestive heart failure (3.4%, including Grade 3 2.3%) were noted.
target_moa: Entrectinib is an inhibitor of ROS1 (ROS proto-oncogene 1 receptor tyrosine kinase), TRKA/B/C (encoded by NTRK1/2/3) and ALK; gene fusions generate fusion oncoproteins that act as dominant drivers of tumorigenesis
companion_dx_detail: Approved without a contemporaneous companion diagnostic; patient selection based on presence of ROS1 rearrangement or NTRK gene fusion, with a PMC to support labeling of a ROS1 detection test

advisory_committee.vote: The Division did not refer this NDA to the Oncologic Drug Advisory Committee (ODAC)

description.text: Expanded to pediatric patients older than 1 month of age with NTRK gene fusion solid tumors and added a new oral suspension route/method of administration for capsules

citations.quote: This Prior Approval sNDA provides for treatment of adult and pediatric patients older than 1 month of age with solid tumors that have a neurotrophic tyrosine receptor kinase (NTRK) gene fusion without a known acquired resistance mutation as detected by an FDA-approved test, are metastatic or where surgical resection is likely to result in severe morbidity, and have progressed following treatment or have no satisfactory alternative therapy, and for a new route and method of administration for capsules prepared as an oral suspension.

surrogate_endpoint.text: For the NTRK gene fusion-positive solid tumor indication: tumor response rate (ORR) and durability of response (DOR); ORR of sufficient magnitude and duration considered reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit

citations.quote: This indication is approved under accelerated approval based on tumor response rate and durability of response [*see Clinical Studies (14.2)*].
FDA generally considers ORR of a sufficient magnitude and duration to be a surrogate endpoint reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit in patients with refractory solid tumors.

confirmatory_requirement.text: Continued approval contingent upon verification and description of clinical benefit in confirmatory trials, including the final report from the first 54 patients with NTRK-fusion solid tumors across ALKA, STARTRK-1 and STARTRK-2

citations.quote: Continued approval for this indication may be contingent upon verification and description of clinical benefit in the confirmatory trials.

Submit the final report, including datasets, from the first 54 patients with *NTRK*-fusion solid tumors enrolled across ALKA, STARTRK-1 [NCT02097810] and STARTRK-2 [NCT02568267] studies to verify and describe the clinical benefit

basis.text: Received breakthrough therapy designation on May 12, 2017 for unresectable or metastatic solid tumors with NTRK-fusion proteins in adults who require systemic therapy and progressed or have no acceptable alternatives

citations.quote: On May 12, 2017, entrectinib received breakthrough therapy designation for the treatment of unresectable or metastatic solid tumors with *NTRK*-fusion proteins in adult patients who require systemic therapy and who have either progressed following prior treatment or who have no acceptable alternative treatments.

orphan_indication.text: Orphan drug designation received February 3, 2015 for TrkA-, TrkB-, TrkC-, ROS1- or ALK-positive NSCLC

citations.quote: February 3, 2015	Entrectinib received orphan drug designation for treatment of TrkA-positive, TrkB-positive, TrkC-positive, ROS1-positive or ALK-positive NSCLC under IND 120500.

Application Number(s)	212725
Priority or Standard	Priority

summary.text: Entrectinib was submitted December 18, 2018 and reviewed under Priority review. The ROS1-positive metastatic NSCLC indication received regular approval based on ORR and DOR from a pooled single-arm efficacy set of 51 patients, while the NTRK gene fusion-positive solid tumor indication received accelerated approval based on tumor response rate and durability of response, with continued approval contingent on confirmatory trials. Entrectinib had received breakthrough therapy designation (May 12, 2017) and orphan drug designation (February 3, 2015).

requirement.text: 3686-1: Determine functional activation or inhibition of off-target receptors, transporters, and/or channels significantly affected by entrectinib or M5 in secondary pharmacology studies

citations.quote: 3686-1 Determine functional activation or inhibition of off-target receptors, transporters, and/or channels that, at concentrations of 10 \muM, showed greater than 50% inhibition by entrectinib or M5 in the secondary pharmacology studies submitted to NDA 212725 and 212726.

requirement.text: 3686-2: Submit integrated safety analyses and supporting data from clinical trials designed to characterize the cardiac risks and sequelae of entrectinib

citations.quote: 3686-2 Submit integrated safety analyses and supporting data from an adequate number of patients enrolled in clinical trial(s) designed to characterize the cardiac risks and sequelae in patients exposed to entrectinib with reasonable precision

requirement.text: 3686-3: Submit integrated safety analyses characterizing the risk of fractures and its sequelae, including serial BMD/DXA assessment

citations.quote: 3686-3 Submit integrated safety analyses and supporting data from an adequate number of patients enrolled in clinical trial(s) designed to characterize the risk of fractures and its sequelae in patients exposed to entrectenib with reasonable precision

requirement.text: 3686-4: Complete a pharmacokinetic trial to evaluate the effect of moderate and severe hepatic impairment on PK and safety of entrectinib

citations.quote: 3686-4 Complete a pharmacokinetic trial to evaluate the effect of moderate and severe hepatic impairment on the pharmacokinetics and safety of Rozlytrek (entrectinib) compared to subjects with normal hepatic function

requirement.text: 3686-5: Submit report further characterizing clinical benefit (BICR ORR and DOR) in 92 ROS1 TKI-naive patients with ROS1-positive NSCLC across ALKA, STARTRK-1 and STARTRK-2

citations.quote: 3686-5 Submit a report, including datasets, of clinical studies that further characterize the clinical benefit of entrectinib for the treatment of adult patients with ROS1 fusion-positive metastatic NSCLC by providing a more precise estimation of the BICR-assessed overall response rate (ORR) and duration of response (DOR) in 92 ROS1 TKI-naive patients with ROS1-positive NSCLC and measurable disease enrolled across the ALKA, STARTRK-1 [NCT02097810] and STARTRK-2 [NCT02568267] studies.

requirement.text: 3686-6: Provide analytical and clinical validation results to support labeling of a test to detect ROS1 rearrangements for identifying patients who may benefit from entrectinib

citations.quote: 3686-6 Commit to providing adequate analytical and clinical validation results from clinical trial data to support labeling of the (b) (4) test to detect ROS1 rearrangements for identifying patients who may benefit from entrectinib.
